en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
Sahadhammika-vagga 82.
The Training Rule on Dedication.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a certain guild in Sāvatthī had prepared a meal together with robes for the Saṅgha, thinking,
"Having fed them, we shall clothe them with robes.
Then the group of six bhikkhus approached that guild.
Having approached, they said this to that group:
"Friends, give these robes to these bhikkhus.
"Venerable sirs, we will not give them."
“An annual alms-offering of robes has been established for our Saṅgha.
“There are many donors for the Saṅgha, friend; there are many supporters of the Saṅgha.
It is by depending on you and out of regard for you that they dwell here.”
“If you do not give these to them, then who indeed will give them?
Give these robes, friends, to these monks.
Then that association, being pressured by the group-of-six monks, gave the robes as prepared to the group-of-six monks and served a meal to the Saṅgha.
Those monks who knew that a meal together with robes had been prepared for the Saṅgha, but did not know that it had been given to the group of six monks, said this:
"Please serve the robes to the Saṅgha, friends. [They replied:
"There are none, venerable sirs."
“The group-of-six noble ladies diverted the robe that had been prepared for them to other group-of-six noble ladies.
Those monks who were few in desires... [and so on]... complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How can the group-of-six monks, knowing that a gain intended for the Saṅgha has been diverted, divert it to an individual?”... [and so on].
“Is it true, monks, that you knowingly diverted to an individual a gain intended for the Saṅgha?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...
"How indeed, you foolish men, can you knowingly divert to an individual a gain that has been dedicated to the Saṅgha?
This, foolish men, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:"
“Whosoever, however, a monk, knowingly diverts to an individual a gain that has been dedicated to the Saṅgha, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Whosoever, however: whosoever of whatever kind... [and so forth].
"Bhikkhu" ...
[as before] ... this is the "bhikkhu" intended in this context.
"Knows" means:
He knows it himself, or others inform him of it, or he informs [the Sangha] himself.
"Belonging to the Sangha" means it has been given to the Sangha and relinquished [to them].
"Gain" means robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites as support for the sick; even down to a lump of powder, a tooth-stick, or a thread for a fringe.
"Transformed" means...
If the speech "We shall give" or "We shall do" has been broken, and she dedicates it to an individual, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If it has been dedicated and she perceives it as having been dedicated, and she dedicates it to an individual, there is an offense of expiation.
If it has been dedicated and she is uncertain of it, and she dedicates it to an individual, there is an offense of wrongdoing (dukkaṭa).
If one has dedicated [something] to an individual, but perceiving it as not dedicated, dedicates it to that individual, there is no offense.
If one dedicates what was dedicated to the Saṅgha to another Saṅgha or to a shrine (cetiya), there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one dedicates what was dedicated to a shrine to another shrine, or to the Saṅgha, or to an individual, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If one diverts what has been dedicated to one person to another person, to the Saṅgha, or to a shrine, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it has not been dedicated and one perceives it as having been dedicated, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it has not been dedicated and one is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense if it has not been transformed and he perceives that it has not been transformed.
There is no offense if, when asked, "Where shall we give it? [he replies:]...

“If he says, ‘Give it where your gift may be used for consumption, or may be used for repairs, or may endure for a long time; or else give it wherever your heart feels confident,’ [there is no offense] for one who is insane or for an initial offender.”
The twelfth training rule on diverting [merit] is finished.
The eighth section, on those of the same Dhamma, is concluded.
Its summary verse:
That which disparages the true Dhamma,
which causes delusion and strikes down,
that which is like a palm-strike and is rootless—
Intentionally eavesdropping,
warding off, consent,
and the dedication of merit.
